paragraphs: Rav Chuna occurs very often in the Jerusalem Talmud. I do not know whether he is the Babylonian Talmud’s Rav Huna; however, we find Huna reporting him and him reporting Huna (see above). Abba son of Rav Chuna (see his entry). Rabbi Avdimi of Tzippori in his name. In Rabbi Adda bar Ahavah’s name: Jerusalem Talmud, Mi Shehotziuhu. Rabbi Uri, Rav Yosef, Rav Yehudah, in Shmuel’s name: beginning of Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot chapter 2. Rabbi Aivu bar Nagri in his name. Rabbi Benay: Midrash Kohelet, on “Do not be overly righteous.” Rabbi Daniel bar Katina in his name. In Rabbi Huna’s name: Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Berakhot chapter 2. Rav Huna in his name: Sanhedrin 3:6. He, Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Pinchas went to Rav Yosef: Jerusalem Talmud, Kiddushin 1:6. Rav Yehudah (see above). Rav Chuna was in the sukkah of Rabbi Yochanan, scribe of Gufta. Rabbi Redifa; Rabbi Yonah in his name: Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Pesachim chapter 8. In Rabbi Yosef’s name: beginning of Shenei Seirim; Ba Lo Kohen Gadol, halakhah 2 (see above). In Rabbi Yirmeyah’s name: beginning of Shekalim chapter 4. Levi bar Panti before him. He objected before Rabbi Mana. Rabbi Mana of Shaav. In Rabbi Nachman bar Yitzchak’s name: Sheviit 3:4. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to him: Megillah chapter 4. Rabbi Pinchas (see above). In Rav’s name: Shekalim chapter 4. Rabbi Redifa (see above). In Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name. Rabbi Shmuel son of Rav Yitzchak in Rabbi Chuna’s name: Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot chapter 2, mishnah 5; Yoma 3:1. That matter in Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 1:2, has Huna instead of Chuna. Shimon Kamtarya. Rabbi Tanchuma in his name: Challah chapter 1.
